question: When `subagent_runs` is empty, `runs.json` remains, and no durable receipt exists, should doctor preserve the source and refuse automatic import, or treat the JSON as authoritative and import it?
rationale: Historical state cannot distinguish a failed-cleanup stale source from a legitimate pre-receipt legacy source, so either automatic policy can change existing users' persisted subagent state.

options.title: Preserve and warn
options.body: Do not import ambiguous JSON automatically; retain it and surface a specific recovery action so stale runs cannot silently return.

options.title: Import legacy JSON
options.body: Treat the retained JSON as authoritative to maximize legacy-run preservation, accepting that a previously imported stale source can resurrect deleted runs.

options.title: Pause for broader migration integration
options.body: Defer this PR until the canonical verified-backup migration service can own ambiguity, recovery, and source cleanup consistently.

recommendation.title: Preserve and warn
recommendation.body: Do not import ambiguous JSON automatically; retain it and surface a specific recovery action so stale runs cannot silently return.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is authorship of the shipped SQLite registry migration and its original cleanup contract.
